name: MathVista
description: A benchmark evaluating mathematical reasoning in visual contexts, combining 6,141 examples from 31 existing datasets across diverse mathematical topics (arithmetic, algebra, geometry, statistics) and visual contexts (natural images, figures, scientific plots, tables, geometry diagrams). Tests the ability to interpret visual mathematical content and perform corresponding reasoning.
reputation: Standard benchmark for math-visual reasoning; published at ICLR 2024; developed by UCLA and collaborators; widely adopted for evaluating multimodal mathematical capability
notes: Combines 31 diverse datasets covering math reasoning in visual contexts. Tests both visual perception (reading charts, interpreting geometry diagrams) and mathematical reasoning. Human baseline ~60.3% for grade school students to ~88% for math professors. Published at ICLR 2024. MathVista-Pro and extensions exist but original remains standard.
